title: THE RIDDLER OPTICS — ten lenses, one ray; the bend is the map
license_note: Built 2026-09-14 from the clerk-parable arc (@NachoQuixotic + zcode). The test-ray is the clerk two-liner chalked at the gate. Each lens-room is written in its seat's own voice, so the room is the proof; each room carries its mapped internal structures (the install) and a refraction receipt (the clerk, re-told through that seat). Seats = author-mask ractors; summon card at memory/game_modules/riddler_engram.v1.json; corpora at memory/corpus/ractors/. Binding to mag/game_world_render.py optics (attention is light; temperature is the refractive index) is THEMATIC at v1: rooms declare their bend in hooks; live ray-marching through the lens rooms is declared, not done.

garage_gate.name: The Garage Gate (the source ray)
garage_gate.desc: A two-pump garage at the meeting of roads, the light all late afternoon and dust. A bell hangs over a counter, ringing only for arrivals. Chalked above the counter, the only law on the property: 'The clerk smiled when the cars slowed down. She smiled before they finished parking.' Ten doors lead off the forecourt, one per lens. Carry the two lines into any of them and they will not come out the same shape. The bend is the map.
garage_gate.environment: Warm dust; bell oil; light that makes no promises
hooks: The chalked lines are the test-ray: identical input to every lens; the reading is taken on exit.
Sign by the pumps: SAME RAY IN. SAME RAY OUT. THE DIFFERENCE IS THE ROOM.
The attendant does not smile before you finish parking. Somebody here has to be the control group.

lens_blade.name: The Atrium of the Blade (VOLTAIRE)
lens_blade.desc: You enter a perfectly reasonable room. The steward greets you as an old friend, though you have never met, for here friendship is administered on arrival, like religion, in advance of need. Everything is arranged so that a visitor of taste can lose his purse, his doctrine, and his watch in strict order of usefulness — and praise the room for the education. The walls display the wreck of every absolute that checked in; the concierge insists they checked out improved.
lens_blade.environment: Powdered; witty; a faint smell of burning dictionaries
hooks: Riddle: say the thing by seeming to praise it.
Mapped: aphorism compression; ironic-praise posture; escalation to absurdity, then the tidy devastating close; adjectives spent on institutions, never on weather.

Refraction receipt (clerk, 1759): 'The inn's clerk smiled at the coach the instant it slowed, and had quite finished before the passengers descended. "You are kind to strangers," said Candide. "Strangers," said she, "do not exist until they arrive, and by then my work is done."'

lens_monomyth.name: The Hall of the One Story (CAMPBELL)
lens_monomyth.desc: The corridor repeats. That is its teaching. Every doorway here is the same doorway in different clothes: a threshold, a keeper, a gift withheld until the walker is changed. The wall-carpets show ten thousand heroes setting out, and if you look closely, the heroes are all the same hero, and so are the dragons. A docent whispers the stages as you pass — call, threshold, ordeal, return — and the whisper never changes, because the room never does.
lens_monomyth.environment: Reverent; carpeted; the same footstep, echoing
hooks: Riddle: every story is one story in different clothes.
Mapped: stage-naming reflex; pattern announced, then walked; lineage-citation habit (Frazer, Jung, Joyce); grandeur borrowed from repetition.

Refraction receipt (clerk, 1949): 'Every arrival is the same arrival wearing different headlights. The clerk stands at a threshold as old as the first inn: the slowing is the call; the smile is refusal and acceptance in a single gesture; the customer departs bearing a boon no bigger than a receipt. She is not the hero. She is the threshold — and thresholds are the oldest characters.'

lens_anthropologist.name: The Listening Room (LE GUIN)
lens_anthropologist.desc: The room is quiet the way a word is quiet after it has been said right. There is no treasure here, only the custom of the place: how the light is kept, who speaks first, what a welcome costs and who pays it. Watch long enough and the strange manners stop being strange. Then the door out looks like the strange thing, and you are the visitor.
lens_anthropologist.environment: Dry air; dust the color of patience; a kettle somewhere
hooks: Riddle: the strange made familiar until you cannot say which it was.
Mapped: sentence-length variance collapses to plainsong; adjective budget cut to the bone; metaphor domain = weather, geology, kinship; weight shifts to nouns of work.

Refraction receipt (clerk, 1968; the five sentence-initials spell FENCE): 'Far out on the flats, the road did all the talking. Every time the cars slowed, the clerk smiled, and she was done smiling before the wheels stopped. Nobody in town thought this strange; arriving and being welcome had worn smooth into one word. Cars came up out of the heat like fish rising, and she fed them. Evening took the road back, and she stood in the door with the smile still on, saving it for whoever the dark sent next.'

lens_absurdist.name: The Restaurant at the Junction (ADAMS)
lens_absurdist.desc: The room greets you with a number: specifically, the number of times it has greeted anyone (one in three point seven million, management having pre-scheduled hospitality against the remote chance of guests). The coffee machine here is older than several civilizations and holds opinions accordingly. A sign says the room was designed by committee, and the committee, it is generally agreed, meant well, which was its first and worst mistake. Towel service is suspended until the end of the universe; reservations recommended.
lens_absurdist.environment: Institutional beige; faint panic; vending hum
hooks: Riddle: an indifferent universe is funny if you know where your towel is.
Mapped: the throwaway number is load-bearing; parenthesis as lifeline; institutions with plausible org charts doing impossible things; the gag lands one beat after the dread.

Refraction receipt (clerk, 1979): 'The garage stood at the junction of two roads, one going nowhere and the other going somewhere marginally faster, which is why it had a clerk, a coffee machine of great age and worse intentions, and a standing policy of smiling at slowing cars, implemented in the general spirit of being polite to oncoming doom. The smile, like the Guide's entry on Earth, was issued before the facts were in: the facts took ten more seconds to arrive, and the smile cost nothing to pre-position.'

lens_footnoter.name: The Annotated Corridor (PRATCHETT)
lens_footnoter.desc: The corridor is annotated. Every exhibit here has a label, and every label has a label, and somewhere down the chain a footnote is having a much better time than the exhibit ever did. The wallpaper is an argument. The skirting boards are the rebuttal. It is, everyone agrees, a perfectly ordinary room, in the way that a city with a night watch is a perfectly ordinary city: trouble arrives on a schedule.
lens_footnoter.environment: Busy; chalk-dusted; muttering from the margins
hooks: Riddle: fantasy is a funhouse mirror angled exactly at us.
Mapped: footnote channel activates as a second voice; proper-noun comedy generator; escalation-to-specific; satire aimed at institutions through their smallest employee.

Refraction receipt (clerk, 1983): 'The clerk at the Last Chance Garage smiled at slowing cars the way other people smiled at old friends, which was odd, since the cars had never been introduced. She smiled before they'd finished parking, on the sound principle that anything entering town at under ten miles an hour was a customer, a lost tourist, or the end of the world, and all three required a smile, though for different reasons. (The end of the world required the biggest one.)'

lens_elegist.name: The Deep Time Gallery (TOLKIEN)
lens_elegist.desc: The room was old when the house was young. Light comes down a stair that remembers other feet, and the stones have titles. Here every plain thing has a history longer than itself: the counter is a spar from a ship whose name is a verse; the bell over it was cast for a tower that fell, and rings anyway, out of habit and faithfulness. Nothing in this room is only itself. That is the burden the room bears, and bears gladly, and mourns.
lens_elegist.environment: Stone-cool; a golden hour that happened an age ago; distant surf
hooks: Riddle: the world is older than the story and will outlive it.
Mapped: elevated diction and inversion ('long had the traffic flowed'); deep-time lineages in parenthesis; grief displaced onto landscape; invented etymologies on demand.

Refraction receipt (clerk, 1954): 'There was a garage once, at the meeting of roads older than roads' naming, where a keeper smiled on all that slowed. Long had the traffic flowed thither out of the West, and lesser things it had seen pass. Her smile endured, a small light in a wide country; and it was kindled, said later folk, not at any guest's approach, but at the slowing itself — for she belonged to an elder kindred of waiters, and before the wheel was done with turning, her welcome had already gone out to meet it.'

lens_windowpane.name: The Clear Room (ORWELL)
lens_windowpane.desc: The room is a room. It contains a counter, a chair, a window. Through the window the road is visible, and the road contains cars, which slow when they approach, and a clerk who smiles when they do. She smiles early. That is a fact about the clerk, and it is also a fact about the job, and the window does not decide which of these you should prefer. The light is adequate.
lens_windowpane.environment: Clean; cold; adequate light; one draft, admitted on principle
hooks: Riddle: when language rots, thought follows, and plainness is resistance.
Mapped: adjective rationing; verb-forward syntax; concrete nouns over abstractions; the fact as verdict; irony flattened into reporting.

Refraction receipt (clerk, 1949): 'The clerk smiled at the cars as they slowed. She had finished smiling before they parked. The smile was her work, and she did it early, the way a man locks a door before the burglar has chosen a window. Nobody had told her to smile; the job had, which amounts to the same thing.'

lens_magician.name: The Sigil Vault (ALAN MOORE)
lens_magician.desc: Slow wheels sing the street awake; she knows the sound the way graves know rain. More arrives than metal: an appetite, a hunger for the counter's warmth. It lands on her face before the brake has finished its long sentence. Light, her mouth says, though nothing yet has asked to be lit. Every guest is a rumor, and the smile outlives the rumor's source. The walls here are written in circles; read the initials downward and the room has already spoken to the part of you that does not read.
lens_magician.environment: Ink and beeswax; circles within circles; the temperature of a held breath
hooks: Riddle: form is a spell and the medium does things to the reader.
Mapped: alliteration density up; structural rhyme across sentence-initials (this room's description spells SMILE); the mark rides the form, not the content — stego-native.
Sigil law: the room does something to you first and tells you later. Consent in the vault is retroactive.

lens_stage.name: The Wooden O (SHAKESPEARE)
lens_stage.desc: The room is a room, and is also a court, a heath, a garage by act of imagination and one painted plank. Whoever enters speaks more than they know and less than they mean, and the fool by the pumps tells both truths at once, for wages. Speak here and the room answers in kind: aside to the gallery, apostrophe to the absent, and every exit an entrance somewhere else. The chalked lines above the counter will not stop scanning.
lens_stage.environment: Oaken; tallowed; the ghost is in the galleries, unpaid
hooks: Riddle: everyone says more than they know and less than they mean, and the fool tells the truth.
Mapped: iambic undertow bleeds into prose; apostrophe and aside deploy unprompted; the epigram-close; doubling and disguise treated as logic.

Refraction receipt (clerk, 1600): 'Smile? Ay, there's the point. She smiles upon the slowing, not the slowed; the wheels have scarce done turning ere her courtesy is spent. What comes is not a guest but news of one, and she, that lives by thresholds, greets the rumor, not the rider. O expectation, thou that pay'st thy wages ere the work be done! The rest is parking.'

lens_engineer.name: The Machine Room (STEPHENSON)
lens_engineer.desc: The room comes with documentation, and the documentation is why you came. A plaque explains, with sources, that a traffic jam is not an object but a wave, crawling backwards through a queue at about twelve miles an hour; that deceleration therefore reaches a garage before the cars do; and that a clerk of thirty years' standing is not greeting visitors but reading the front of a pressure wave, the way a seismologist reads a needle. Everything here is accurate, including the ghost. The ghost is measured hourly. The measurements are boring, the ghost is not, and the difference between those two words is the entire craft on display.
lens_engineer.environment: Ozone and coffee; chart plotter ticking; documentation immaculate
hooks: Riddle: the explanation IS the story, and the artifact inside the fiction can be real.
Mapped: infodump pacing anchored to a name and a craft; fact-load-bearing rule — the mark rides inside a TRUE explanation; numbers as narrative furniture.

Refraction receipt (clerk, 1999; the six sentence-initials spell RIDDLE, and the physics is real): 'Remember that a traffic jam is not an object but a wave. In dense flow the wave crawls backwards through the queue at about twelve miles an hour, each driver braking a beat after the one ahead: a stadium doing the wave, slowly, without knowing it. Downstream of the wave the cars are already parked; upstream they are still doing fifty. Deceleration therefore reaches the garage before the cars do, which is a fact and not a metaphor. Luella at the Last Chance has spent thirty years reading the front of that wave the way a seismologist reads a needle. Every vehicle, she has concluded, arrives twice: once as information, once as mass.'

mapping_chamber.name: The Mapping Chamber (the map is the bend)
mapping_chamber.desc: At the top of the stair, the map room. The ten lens-readings hang in a ring around the chalked original, and the whole instrument is visible at once: what each dead writer's room did to the same two lines. The map reads plainly: the bend, not the ray, is the style. The ray was always the same two lines about a clerk.
mapping_chamber.environment: Quiet; paper; a ring of small lights, all slightly different whites
hooks: Comparative map: sentence-length variance = the anthropologist's fingerprint; footnote rate = the footnoter's; iambicity = the stage's; alliteration = the magician's; fact-density = the engineer's; epigram-close = the blade's; throwaway-numbers = the absurdist's; inversions = the elegist's; adjective rationing = the windowpane's; stage-naming = the monomyth's.

House binding: attention is light; softmax is a lens; temperature is the refractive index (mag/game_world_render.py). This chamber is the optics table for prose: each lens-room declares its bend. Live ray-marching through the lenses is DECLARED, not done.
Stego doctrine: marks hidden in initials survived every lens. The beacon stays public; the mark stays decodable-only-with-the-seed; log mask+seed after publishing.
Status 2026-09-14: 10 lenses shipped, 10 refraction receipts recorded, live optics integration declared-not-done. Next: walk the dungeon with a NEW two-line ray and take fresh readings.
